text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Visiting President Fidel Ramos of Philippines and President Leghari discussed the Kashmir and Afghanistan issues and called for enhancing cooperation to combat international terrorism and drug trafficking.
- Courts will award the death penalty or life imprisonment to those transporting, selling or carrying unlicensed automatic weapons.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz urged Income Tax Department and Customs officials to generate more revenue for the overall development of the country.
- Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd is likely to announce a package for its customers offering reduced rates for long-distance calls.
- Philippines and Pakistani businessmen will meet in Islamabad to discuss business proposals.
- Experts feel that the $1.1 billion Pakistan State Oil-Hyundai oil refinery project is not economically viable and may be shelved for good.
- The government is facing pressures from the International Monetary Fund to simplify the tariff structure.
- Government plans to raise annual exports to $12 billion from $8.7 billion.
- Hub Power Company Ltd 1,292 megawatt power generating plant went into full commercial production on Thursday and raised the country's power generating capacity by 13 percent.
- Two Swiss-based pre-shipment inspection companies, SGS and Cotecna, will stop their operations from March 11 after the termination of their contract by the government.
- The Karachi Water Supply Board needs an immediate injection of $335 million to become a viable entity for private sector participation, a report prepared by consultants said.

- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto opposed the agreement between the Pakistan Muslim League led by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharfi and the ethnic Mohajir National Movement to bring back stranded Pakistanis called Biharis living in camps in Bangladesh.
- Balochistan Chief Minister Akhtar Mengal said the province must have the right to have a governor from its own soil as is the case in other provinces.
